entries.title: Gerber Rice Cereal (baby food)
entries.result: Inorganic arsenic averaged 63 ppb. At one serving a day that is above Consumer Reports' level of concern. They suggest limiting to half a serving a day.
entries.threshold: Consumer Reports compares one serving with the strictest health-based limits it could find. The FDA action level for infant rice cereal is 100 ppb and is not mandatory. Consumer Reports has long argued that limit is too high.
caveats: Results are a snapshot. Makers can change ingredients and processes at any time.
Averages of two to four lots bought anonymously. Other lots may differ.
Consumer Reports says its findings are guidance, not legal judgments or compliance findings.
entries.response: Gerber says its products meet all applicable FDA limits and its own standards.
entries.ties: Tester funding and ties: not checked yet.

entries.title: Good & Gather Baby Fruit Purée, Banana, Peach & Apricot (Target)
entries.result: Inorganic arsenic was 5.7 ppb, above Consumer Reports' level of concern. They suggest limiting to one serving a day.
entries.threshold: The FDA has not finalized guidance for inorganic arsenic in baby food purées.
caveats: Results are a snapshot. Makers can change ingredients and processes at any time.
Averages of two to four lots bought anonymously. Other lots may differ.
Consumer Reports says its findings are guidance, not legal judgments or compliance findings.
entries.response: Target says it requires vendors to meet all applicable requirements.

entries.title: Baby Mum-Mum Banana Teething Wafers
entries.result: Heavy metals were below Consumer Reports' level of concern, but BPA was comparatively high in all three lots tested. They suggest no more than half a serving a week.
entries.threshold: Bisphenol limits are based on the most protective exposure limits Consumer Reports could find.
caveats: Results are a snapshot. Makers can change ingredients and processes at any time.
Averages of two to four lots bought anonymously. Other lots may differ.
Consumer Reports says its findings are guidance, not legal judgments or compliance findings.
entries.response: The company says its testing is risk-based and covers packaging and raw materials.
entries.ties: Tester funding and ties: not checked yet.

entries.title: Naked Nutrition Vegan Mass Gainer (vanilla)
entries.result: Lead was 7.7 micrograms per serving, about 1,570% of Consumer Reports' level of concern. They advise against using it.
entries.threshold: Level of concern for lead: 0.5 micrograms a day, based on California's Prop 65 limit. The trade group Council for Responsible Nutrition called this level misleading.
caveats: Results are a snapshot. Makers can change ingredients and processes at any time.
Averages of two to four lots bought anonymously. Other lots may differ.
Consumer Reports says its findings are guidance, not legal judgments or compliance findings.
entries.response: The company says it sources from suppliers that document heavy-metal checks and has requested a third-party test.
entries.ties: Tester funding and ties: not checked yet.

entries.title: Huel Black Edition (chocolate)
entries.result: Lead was 6.3 micrograms per serving (about 1,290% of the level of concern) and cadmium was 9.2 micrograms, more than double the 4.1 microgram daily level. They advise against using it.
entries.threshold: Level of concern for lead: 0.5 micrograms a day (California Prop 65). Cadmium: 4.1 micrograms a day.
caveats: Results are a snapshot. Makers can change ingredients and processes at any time.
Averages of two to four lots bought anonymously. Other lots may differ.
Consumer Reports says its findings are guidance, not legal judgments or compliance findings.
entries.response: Huel says its ingredients are rigorously tested and within levels set out by NSF. It did not answer questions about the cadmium.
entries.ties: Tester funding and ties: not checked yet.

entries.title: Protein powders as a category
entries.result: Of 160 top-selling protein powders from 70 brands, 47% exceeded at least one federal or state limit, including California's Prop 65. 21% were over twice the Prop 65 lead level. Plant-based and chocolate products had the highest levels.
entries.threshold: Federal and state limits, including California Prop 65.
caveats: This describes the category, not the product in front of you.
Results depend on the products and thresholds the tester chose.

source.label: Clean Label Project, protein powder study (2025)

entries.ties: Tester ties to check: Clean Label Project also runs a paid-for certification program for brands. Other funding not checked yet.

entries.title: Packaged baby foods as a category
entries.result: Of 48 baby foods from 11 brands, 96% were below Consumer Reports' level of concern for heavy metals. Inorganic arsenic was detected in 77%, cadmium in 80% and lead in 85%. Phthalates were found in 81%, and microplastics in all 15 purées tested for them.
entries.threshold: Consumer Reports' level of concern, based on the strictest health-based limits it could find.
caveats: This describes the category, not the product in front of you.
Consumer Reports says microplastics have no regulatory limits and their health effects are still being studied.
entries.ties: Tester funding and ties: not checked yet.
